newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares slide again, Olivetti suspended.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares slide again, Olivetti suspended.

text.p: Italian shares slipped to a lower close on Wednesday weighed down by a corruption probe, a lower Wall Street, the continuing crisis at stuggling Olivetti and a general lack of buying interest, dealers and analysts said.

Olivetti recovered dramatically once trading in the shares got underway but was soon suspended at the 10 percent limit up level. Olivetti gave answers to 16 Consob questions but analysts said these gave little fresh information. Attention now focuses on a Olivetti board meeting due to start at 1600 GMT.
The all-share Mibtel index ended down 0.75 percent at 9,516 and Mib30 blue chip index off 0.73 percent at 14,233.

The corruption probe involving the head of the state railways Lorenzo Necci saw new development on Wednesday when magistrates indicated major political figures might also be caught up in affair. This was denied by the chief prosecutor.

Dealers said that attention on Olivetti was focused on the group's board meeting where market talk suggested that the company's chief executive Francesco Caio could be replaced after less than three months at the helm.
Olivetti shares were last quoted up 9.61 percent at 510 lire after hitting record lows on Tuesday. The shares failed to re-start trading after suspension on Wednesday.
Oil group ENI ended off 1.13 percent at 6,922 lire after first half 1996 profits on Tuesday came largely in line with expectations, but many analysts had been looking for figures to exceed forecasts.
Gemina was one share to stand out rising 8.65 percent to 714.5 lire after the financial holding group reporting a return to the black in the first half of 1996 late Tuesday.

Fiat ended off 1.78 percent at 4,191 lire ahead of its first half results on Thursday, expected to show a fall due to heavy investment in new vehicle models and a continued depressed Italian car market.
